title: Gukesh Visits Tirumala Temple Ahead of World Chess Championship Title Defence
excerpt: The 20-year-old world champion offered prayers at Tirumala on November 6 before facing Javokhir Sindarov in a 14-game title match in Geneva from November 24 to December 12.
body:
• World champion D Gukesh, 20, offered prayers at the Tirumala Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple in Andhra Pradesh on Friday, November 6, ahead of his title defence.
  • He defends his crown against Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov in a 14-game classical match in Geneva from November 24 to December 12; the first player to 7.5 points wins, with a $2.5 million prize fund.
  • Both players will be 20 when the match begins, making it the youngest World Championship battle in chess history.
  • The harder story is form: FIDE's own preview notes Gukesh has slipped to 26th on the rating list at 2710 Elo, while Sindarov arrives off a 2025 World Cup win and victory in the April 2026 Candidates.

Reigning World Chess Champion D Gukesh visited the Tirumala Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple in Andhra Pradesh on Friday, November 6, to offer prayers ahead of his FIDE World Chess Championship title defence, ANI reported. The 20-year-old grandmaster sought blessings at the shrine atop the Tirumala hills in Tirupati district, dedicated to Lord Venkateswara. The visit came just days after he had also visited Neem Karoli Baba's ashram, as his preparations for the biggest match of his career enter their final weeks.

The match he is preparing for

Gukesh defends his crown against Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov in a 14-game classical match from November 24 to December 12 at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny, Geneva, Switzerland. The opening ceremony is on November 22 and the first game on November 24; the final classical game is scheduled for December 11, with a tiebreak on December 12 if the score is level at 7-7. The first player to reach 7.5 points is champion. The total prize fund is $2.5 million. Because both Gukesh and Sindarov will be 20 years old when the match begins, it will be the youngest World Championship battle in chess history.

The title he is defending

Gukesh won the championship in December 2024 in Singapore, defeating China's Ding Liren 7.5-6.5 in a match decided in the fourteenth and final game. At 18 years, six months and 24 days, he became the youngest undisputed World Chess Champion in history, breaking a record Garry Kasparov had held for more than four decades, and only the second Indian to win the title after Viswanathan Anand. The Chennai-born champion had become a grandmaster in January 2019 at 12 years, seven months and 17 days, and was the youngest player to cross the 2750 rating mark and India's top-rated player by September 2023.

Why this defence is different

FIDE's own preview, published by ChessBase, frames the defence bluntly: Gukesh must rediscover his best form. Since around the middle of 2025, his results have grown increasingly inconsistent, and he has slipped to 26th place in the FIDE rating list with 2710 Elo points — an unusual position for a reigning champion. Sindarov, by contrast, arrives with momentum, having won the 2025 World Cup before dominating the Candidates Tournament in April 2026 to earn this match. FIDE notes that Gukesh has reportedly sought time for reflection and preparation in recent months, with the Tirumala visit in early November attracting attention. His strengths, the federation adds, remain intact: opening versatility, exceptional calculating ability, resilience under pressure and a record of rising to the occasion, from the Candidates to the final game in Singapore.

What to watch

For chess fans in India and the diaspora, the Geneva match is a three-week story with a clear shape: whether the champion's preparation — and the quieter weeks that included Tirumala — has restored the form of 2024. Game 1 is on November 24, and the match cannot end before one player reaches 7.5 points, so every early result shifts the pressure onto the other side of the board.
